ECON 123.description: Basic concepts, institutional foundations, structure of the private and public sector, labor markets; major economic problems.
ECON 123.subject: ECON
ECON 123.title: The American Economy

ECON 221.description: The study of supply and demand, pricing and cost concepts, firm and consumer decision-making, market structure, and government policies.
ECON 221.subject: ECON
ECON 221.title: Principles of Microeconomics

ECON 222.description: The study of gross domestic product, business cycles, economic growth, inflation, unemployment, and monetary and fiscal policy.
ECON 222.subject: ECON
ECON 222.title: Principles of Macroeconomics

ECON 223.description: Introduction to economics principles for non-majors. Basics of supply and demand and government and monetary policy are covered in a non-technical manner. Not open to business or economics students. Credit not granted for both ECON 223 and ECON 221 or ECON 222 .
ECON 223.subject: ECON
ECON 223.title: Introduction to Economics

ECON 224.description: The study of supply and demand, markets, household and firm decision-making, gross domestic product, inflation, unemployment, and government policies. Open to all students except business administration and economics majors.
ECON 224.subject: ECON
ECON 224.title: Introduction to Economics

ECON 301.description: The role of money in the market economy. Commercial banks, the Federal Reserve System, and monetary policy. Cannot be used to satisfy major requirements.
ECON 301.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 301.subject: ECON
ECON 301.title: Money and Banking

ECON 303.description: Survey of international economic issues and institutions, including trade and protectionism, global and regional trade agreements, trade balances and exchange rates, Japan, NAFTA, and the European Union.
ECON 303.subject: ECON
ECON 303.title: The International Economy

ECON 311.description: The nature and causes of major economic problems facing the nation and its communities, and policy alternatives designed to solve them. The philosophy and methodology of economics in social problem solving.
ECON 311.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 311.subject: ECON
ECON 311.title: Issues in Economics

ECON 316.description: Applications of economic theory to sports through hands-on analysis of data from sporting events and other sports markets.
ECON 316.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 221 and ECON 222; or C or better in ECON 224.
ECON 316.subject: ECON
ECON 316.title: Sports Economics

ECON 321.description: Analysis of the economic behavior of households and firms. Production, consumption, price determination, and the degree of competition in markets.
ECON 321.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224, MATH 122 or MATH 141.
ECON 321.subject: ECON
ECON 321.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory

ECON 322.description: Analysis of the national economy as a whole. Money, output, employment, inflation, and international economic linkages.
ECON 322.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224, MATH 122 or MATH 141.
ECON 322.subject: ECON
ECON 322.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Theory

ECON 329.description: Growth and development of the American economy; applications of economic theory to economic history.
ECON 329.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 329.subject: ECON
ECON 329.title: American Economic History

ECON 336.description: An introduction to the various types and sources of data used by economists and how to interpret such data to answer economic questions and support economic theory. Includes the uses of survey data, cross-sectional, time series, and panel data.
ECON 336.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 221 and ECON 222 or ECON 224.
ECON 336.subject: ECON
ECON 336.title: Introduction to Data Science for Economists

ECON 363.description: The procurement and management of wealth by privately owned profit-seeking enterprises.
ECON 363.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221, ACCT 225, and 3 hours of statistics at the 200-level.
ECON 363.subject: ECON
ECON 363.title: Business Finance

ECON 364.description: A study of the functions and operations of financial institutions and their relationships to the commercial banking system and the general economy. Attention is devoted to savings institutions, insurance companies, rural and urban real estate credit, consumer credit, and associated topics.
ECON 364.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 364.subject: ECON
ECON 364.title: Financial Institutions

ECON 379.description: An analysis of public policy toward business in the United States. Emphasis is on the desirability of various policies in light of their consequences for the general welfare.
ECON 379.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 379.subject: ECON
ECON 379.title: Government Policy Toward Business

ECON 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and undergraduate division head is required.
ECON 399.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 399.subject: ECON
ECON 399.title: Independent Study

ECON 402.description: A study of monetary standards, monetary theory, monetary policy, and the mechanism of international payments. Attention is devoted to questions of monetary problems, employment, and fiscal policy.
ECON 402.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 402.subject: ECON
ECON 402.title: Money, Income, and Prices

ECON 406.description: A study of labor market institutions, trends in labor market activity, and the effects of government policy on the labor market. (Not open to majors in economics.)
ECON 406.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 406.subject: ECON
ECON 406.title: Labor Economics

ECON 408.description: A survey of economics from the ancient philosophers to the present; with emphasis on the mercantilist, physiocratic, classical, Marxian, Austrian, neo-classical, and institutional schools of economics.
ECON 408.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 408.subject: ECON
ECON 408.title: History of Economic Thought

ECON 415.description: A study of the structure of selected American industries, of the development and concentration of economic power in the American economy, and of public policy toward industry.
ECON 415.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 415.subject: ECON
ECON 415.title: Economics of American Industry

ECON 420.description: Analysis of business cycles and applications of forecasting techniques to project and interpret economic trends.
ECON 420.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 420.subject: ECON
ECON 420.title: Business Applications of Economic Forecasting

ECON 421.description: Decision making with respect to capital goods, with emphasis on such decision making in governmental activities and public utilities. Intended primarily for engineering students, the course emphasizes the types of investment decisions that engineers are often called upon to make.
ECON 421.subject: ECON
ECON 421.title: Engineering Economics

ECON 436.description: The use of statistical techniques to analyze economic relationships. The emphasis is on the application of linear regression to real-world economic data.
ECON 436.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 224, or ECON 221 and ECON 222; MGSC 291 or STAT 201; and MATH 122 or MATH 141.
ECON 436.subject: ECON
ECON 436.title: Introductory Econometrics

ECON 476.description: Examines the foundations of capitalism and why it has prevailed over alternative systems. Topics include the justification of private property, distribution of wealth, profit motive, source of wealth creation, and others.
ECON 476.subject: ECON
ECON 476.title: Foundations of Capitalism

ECON 499.description: Supervised work experience of at least nine hours per week, to include one class meeting a month and individual consultation. Contract approval by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required. Cannot be used to satisfy major requirement.
ECON 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in both ECON 321 and ECON 322, and cumulative GPA of 2.75.
ECON 499.subject: ECON
ECON 499.title: Internship in Economics

ECON 500.description: An analysis of economic forces affecting urbanization and the economic processes influencing urban form and structure. Spatial concepts are considered in addition to traditional micro-economic and macro-economic concepts. Topic coverage includes: the economic origin of cities; urban functions and the urban economic base, land-use structure and urban form, and urban efficiency.
ECON 500.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 500.subject: ECON
ECON 500.title: Urban Economics

ECON 503.description: Theory of international specialization, commercial policy, customs unions, and the effects of trade liberalization and protectionism; economic growth and multinational enterprises.
ECON 503.subject: ECON
ECON 503.title: International Trade Economics

ECON 504.description: Exchange rate and balance of payments determination; purchasing-power parity; optimum currency areas, absorption, elasticity, monetary approaches, spot- and forward-exchange markets.
ECON 504.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 322.
ECON 504.subject: ECON
ECON 504.title: International Monetary Economics

ECON 505.description: Economic theories of growth in developing countries. Use of factor resources; role of social and economic institutions; use of financial trade policies for growth.
ECON 505.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 505.subject: ECON
ECON 505.title: International Development Economics

ECON 506.description: Economics of labor demand, labor supply, wage determination in competitive markets, migration, discrimination, unemployment, and labor unions. Theoretical models and empirical knowledge will be considered.
ECON 506.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224; ECON 321.
ECON 506.subject: ECON
ECON 506.title: Labor Economics and Labor Markets

ECON 507.description: An analysis of the organization and operation of the world’s major economic systems.
ECON 507.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 507.subject: ECON
ECON 507.title: Comparative Economic Systems

ECON 508.description: Economic analysis and interpretation of the law. The economic effect of current law and optimal design of law to meet social objectives.
ECON 508.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 508.subject: ECON
ECON 508.title: Law and Economics

ECON 509.description: Exploration of the basic theory and practice of sustainable economic development. Topics include: environmental legislation, global agreements, sustainable development indicators, and economic strategies and methods to promote environmentally sound development.
ECON 509.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in the following ECON 221 and ECON 222; or ECON 224; MATH 122.
ECON 509.subject: ECON
ECON 509.title: Economics of Sustainable Development

ECON 510.description: Exploration of the basic theory and techniques of experimental economics. Topics include: basic game theory, experimental design, and elements of behavioral economic thought.
ECON 510.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in ECON 321.
ECON 510.subject: ECON
ECON 510.title: Experimental Economics

ECON 511.description: Philosophy and methodology of economics, perspectives on theory and empiricism, economic policy; individualized guided research.
ECON 511.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 321, ECON 322, and ECON 436 with grade of C or higher.
ECON 511.subject: ECON
ECON 511.title: Senior Seminar in Economics

ECON 514.description: Focuses on the following aspects of terrorism: (1) its causes/determinants (historical, social, cultural, economic, political, and religious determinants); (2) the organizational and funding structure of terrorist groups; (3) the tactics and weapons of terrorist groups; (4) mobilization and recruitment within terror networks; and (5) counterterrorism methods. Restricted to: Business Majors and Economics Arts and Sciences Majors.
ECON 514.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 321.
ECON 514.subject: ECON
ECON 514.title: The Economics of Terrorism

ECON 515.description: This course uses the tools of microeconomics and game theory to examine how firms compete and competition’s impact on industry performance. Topics include: price discrimination, product differentiation, and oligopoly behavior.
ECON 515.subject: ECON
ECON 515.title: Industrial Organization

ECON 516.description: This course covers fundamental models of collective decision making, studies their empirical relevance, and considers interactions between the economy and politics.
ECON 516.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 221 and ECON 222 or C or better in ECON 224.
ECON 516.subject: ECON
ECON 516.title: Political Economy

ECON 520.description: This seminar course is designed to introduce students who have been accepted into the Econ Scholars program to economics research and real-world problem solving.
ECON 520.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in ECON 321, ECON 322, and ECON 436.
ECON 520.subject: ECON
ECON 520.title: Economic Scholars I

ECON 521.description: This seminar course continues the work from Econ Scholars I and is reserved for students who have been accepted into the Econ Scholars program. Students will be placed in teams and partnered with local businesses, government agencies, or economics faculty members to work on real-world projects and academic research.
ECON 521.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in ECON 520.
ECON 521.subject: ECON
ECON 521.title: Economic Scholars II

ECON 523.description: Mathematical formulation of economic theories; the use of mathematics in the development and demonstration of economic relationships.
ECON 523.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224; MATH 122, MATH 141, or the equivalent.
ECON 523.subject: ECON
ECON 523.title: Introduction to Mathematical Economics

ECON 524.description: A course designed to acquaint the student with the principles of operation of the American economic system. A survey course for social studies teachers in secondary schools.
ECON 524.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 524.subject: ECON
ECON 524.title: Essentials of Economics

ECON 526.description: A study of the application of the economic theory of profits, competition, demand, and costs to analysis of problems arising in the firm and in decision making. Price policies, forecasting, and investment decisions are among the topics considered.
ECON 526.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 526.subject: ECON
ECON 526.title: Managerial Economics

ECON 530.description: Investment in human capital; the economic value of schooling; internal efficiency of schools; faculty compensation; equity and efficiency of school finance systems; financing higher education.
ECON 530.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 530.subject: ECON
ECON 530.title: The Economics of Education

ECON 531.description: Applications of economic analysis to health care. Structure and behavior of health-care markets. Description of health care policy issues.
ECON 531.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 531.subject: ECON
ECON 531.title: Health Economics

ECON 532.description: Applications of economic analysis to early childhood. Topics may include research and policy related to families, pregnancy, birth, and early childhood.
ECON 532.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in ECON 221, ECON 224, or equivalent; C or higher in STAT 201, STAT 206, or equivalent with a grade of C or higher.
ECON 532.subject: ECON
ECON 532.title: Research and Policy from Birth to Kindergarten

ECON 548.description: An analysis of the economics aspects of environmental decay, pollution control, and natural resource use. Analysis of the ability of the market system to allocate resources efficiently when economic activity is accompanied by environmental damage. Discussion of alternative public policy approaches to pollution control and natural resource conservation.
ECON 548.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 221 and ECON 222 or C or better in ECON 224.
ECON 548.subject: ECON
ECON 548.title: Environmental Economics

ECON 555.description: Game theory as used to understand decision making in business, economics, politics and other real-world environments. Topics covered include: basic terminology; strategic, extensive, and combinatorial models; and equilibrium strategy.
ECON 555.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 321 or MATH 141 and STAT 201 or C or higher in STAT 206.
ECON 555.subject: ECON
ECON 555.title: Game Theory in Economics

ECON 562.description: Theory and practice of taxation: public revenue, expenditure, and debt.
ECON 562.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in ECON 321.
ECON 562.subject: ECON
ECON 562.title: Public Finance

ECON 589.description: Individual topics to be announced with title.
ECON 589.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 589.subject: ECON
ECON 589.title: Topics in Economics

ECON 594.description: Advanced econometric methods including quasi-experimental methods, applications of machine learning to causal inference and economic forecasting, and related topics.
ECON 594.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 436.
ECON 594.subject: ECON
ECON 594.title: Advanced Econometrics

ECON 621.description: Neo-classical value and distribution theory combined with income and employment theory.
ECON 621.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 621.subject: ECON
ECON 621.title: Survey of Contemporary Economic Theory

ECON 690.description: Calculus and classical optimization methods applied to problems in business and economic analysis; matrices, derivatives, and integrals in the analysis of both univariate and multivariate business and economic models.
ECON 690.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 690.subject: ECON
ECON 690.title: Quantitative Foundations for Business and Economics I

ECON 691.description: Statistics and probability theory applied to problems of business and economic analysis.
ECON 691.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224; MGSC 690 or ECON 690.
ECON 691.subject: ECON
ECON 691.title: Quantitative Foundations for Business and Economics II

ECON 692.description: Probability and statistics necessary for graduate study in economics and business administration; estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, analysis of variance, and nonparametric methods.
ECON 692.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
ECON 692.subject: ECON
ECON 692.title: Quantitative Methods I

ECON 694.description: A study of decision models useful in business administration. Topics covered include linear programming, sensitivity analysis and duality, network models, integer programming, determinate and stochastic dynamic programming, inventory, and queues.
ECON 694.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224; ECON 692, mathematics and computer portion of Fundamental Business Skills or equivalent.
ECON 694.subject: ECON
ECON 694.title: Quantitative Methods II

ECON 705.description: Overall view of problems of economic development, including its history and relationship to the modern world. Brief consideration is given to such noneconomic factors as political, sociological, and cultural environments. Basic theories of growth are presented and critically evaluated.
ECON 705.subject: ECON
ECON 705.title: Economic Growth and Development

ECON 711.description: Theory of demand, production, cost, pricing, distribution, and capital. Particular emphasis on applications of the theory to various problems faced by the firm.
ECON 711.subject: ECON
ECON 711.title: Applied Microeconomics

ECON 712.description: The modern theory of income determination. Inflation, unemployment, and interest rates in an open economy setting. Emphasis on economic policy.
ECON 712.subject: ECON
ECON 712.title: Applied Macroeconomics

ECON 719.description: The modern theory of national employment, output, and the price level. Monetary and fiscal policy. International trade, exchange rates, and international capital markets.
ECON 719.subject: ECON
ECON 719.title: Macroeconomics Analysis and International Economics

ECON 720.description: The application of microeconomic concepts to managerial decisions. The concepts include demand, cost, market structure, pricing, profitability, and strategic behavior.
ECON 720.subject: ECON
ECON 720.title: Managerial Economics

ECON 727.description: The MA Econ practicum course involves developing and executing a team-based project in applied economics. The course is broken down into sections to help each team maintain progress on their project and culminates in a day of project presentations open to the public. The instructor will provide general and specific guidance throughout. Team are encouraged to partner with businesses or government in developing their project, but may also choose a topic independently.
ECON 727.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in ECON 711, ECON 712, and ECON 736.
ECON 727.subject: ECON
ECON 727.title: MA Economics Practicum

ECON 728.description: Theory of demand, production, cost, pricing, distribution, and capital. Particular emphasis on applications of the theory to various problems faced by the firm.
ECON 728.subject: ECON
ECON 728.title: Applied Microeconomics

ECON 736.description: The theory and application of linear regression analysis to economic problems. The course will present both finite-sample and asymptotic properties of regression estimators, and address problems that arise in using regression methods with economic data.
ECON 736.subject: ECON
ECON 736.title: Applied Econometrics

ECON 740.description: Examination of a variety of techniques that are used for forecasting and policy simulation purposes. Development of skills that have applications in business, government, and economic research.
ECON 740.subject: ECON
ECON 740.title: Applied Economic Forecasting

ECON 760.description: Classical and modern models of international trade, evaluation of tariffs and quotas, advantages and disadvantages of international trade agreements.
ECON 760.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 711 or ECON 720, with exceptions made for anyone who has taken an undergraduate Intermediate Microeconomics class ECON 321 at USC in the last five years.
ECON 760.subject: ECON
ECON 760.title: International Trade, Theory and Policy

ECON 784.description: A critical introduction to the application of economic analysis to problems in the health care field. Selective surveys of the related scientific literature will be covered.
ECON 784.subject: ECON
ECON 784.title: Health Economics

ECON 794.description: Mathematical programming techniques which are useful in business and economics. Topics include: solution techniques and applications of linear programming, duality, theory, parametric programming, the decomposition problem, integer programming, dynamic programming, Lagrange multipliers, Kuhn-Tucker theory, and an introduction to control theory.
ECON 794.subject: ECON
ECON 794.title: Programming Methods

ECON 798.description: Directed research on a topic to be developed by MS Economics student and instructor. May be repeated.
ECON 798.subject: ECON
ECON 798.title: Economics Independent Study

ECON 811.description: The modern theory of consumer behavior, production, the firm, and market structure.
ECON 811.subject: ECON
ECON 811.title: Microeconomic Theory I

ECON 812.description: Advanced topics in microeconomics including general equilibrium theory and welfare economics.
ECON 812.subject: ECON
ECON 812.title: Microeconomic Theory II

ECON 814.description: This course teaches the fundamentals of game theory and strategic interaction. Concepts of normal and extensive form games, Nash Equilibrium, and subgame perfect equilibrium are defined and used to show how outcomes are achieved between two parties.
ECON 814.subject: ECON
ECON 814.title: Game Theory

ECON 815.description: Examination of new theories and applications in microeconomics. Analysis of advances in theory and the application of theory to new new problems of consumer behaviour, industrial organization, and public economics.
ECON 815.subject: ECON
ECON 815.title: Topics in Microeconomics

ECON 816.description: This course is to acquaint students with the mathematical methods currently being used in micro- and macroeconomic theory. Topics covered are the use in economics of point set topology, nonlinear programming, differential equations, calculus of variations, and control theory.
ECON 816.subject: ECON
ECON 816.title: Mathematical Economics

ECON 817.description: An analysis of the development of economic theory with special emphasis on the evolution of alternative methodologies.
ECON 817.subject: ECON
ECON 817.title: History of Economic Thought

ECON 818.description: An endeavor to formulate propositions by which alternative economic situations open to society may be ranked on the scale of better or worse.
ECON 818.subject: ECON
ECON 818.title: Welfare Economics

ECON 821.description: The modern theories of income determination, inflation, unemployment, and interest rates. Theories of consumption, investment, government expenditure, and taxation are presented.
ECON 821.subject: ECON
ECON 821.title: Macroeconomic Theory I

ECON 822.description: Recent developments in macro-econometrics, dynamic models, and related topics.
ECON 822.subject: ECON
ECON 822.title: Macroeconomic Theory II

ECON 824.description: Monetary theory, monetary policy, and monetary reform. Theory of central banking and monetary equilibrium, and related topics.
ECON 824.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: course in money and banking and intermediate economic theory.
ECON 824.subject: ECON
ECON 824.title: Monetary Theory

ECON 825.description: An in-depth study of the operation and economic significance of the monetary system (money, commercial banks, and the central bank) and monetary policy. Emphasis is on theory and empirical hypothesis testing as related to above topics.
ECON 825.subject: ECON
ECON 825.title: Money and Banking

ECON 831.description: A treatment of single equation estimating techniques for the simple linear model, various nonlinear models, and the general linear model.
ECON 831.subject: ECON
ECON 831.title: Econometrics and Regression I

ECON 832.description: Topics in generalized least squares, autocorrelation, distributed lag models, principal components, identification, and simultaneous estimating techniques.
ECON 832.subject: ECON
ECON 832.title: Econometrics and Regression II

ECON 833.description: Theory and application of computational methods used to solve and estimate economic models. Solutions to economic models using numerical techniques and high-performance computing. Estimation of empirical models using custom built functions and numerical optimization.
ECON 833.subject: ECON
ECON 833.title: Computational Methods for Economists

ECON 840.description: Advanced theory of economic growth. Mathematical models of growth, including the neoclassical model, endogenous growth models, and models of imperfect competition and growth, will be examined. Techniques of dynamic optimization are used to solve models. Empirical methods will be applied to models of economic growth.
ECON 840.subject: ECON
ECON 840.title: Economic Growth

ECON 841.description: Application of economic principles to regional analysis and planning. Geographic areas covered range from cities and counties to major regions of the nation. Subject areas include economic measurement, analysis, and development planning.
ECON 841.subject: ECON
ECON 841.title: Economic Development

ECON 843.description: Examination and interpretation of the record of events and trends in history usingthe concepts and tools of economic theory. Analysis of the effect of economic events on the course of world history.
ECON 843.subject: ECON
ECON 843.title: Economic History

ECON 848.description: Fundamentals of environmental and resource economics. Including concepts of pollution, instrument choice, management of renewable and non-renewable resources, and valuation techniques for environmental public goods.
ECON 848.subject: ECON
ECON 848.title: Environmental Economics

ECON 850.description: A critical introduction to the application of economic analysis to problems in the health care field. Selective surveys of the related scientific literature will be covered.
ECON 850.subject: ECON
ECON 850.title: Health Economics

ECON 860.description: Theory of international values, comparative advantage, and the gains from trade; theory of commercial policy, tariff structure, and welfare and trade.
ECON 860.subject: ECON
ECON 860.title: International Trade Theory

ECON 862.description: Theories of exchange rate and balance of payments determination (spot and forward exchange markets, interest rate arbitage, purchasing power parity, and monetary approaches); adjustments under fixed and flexible exchange rates are analyzed.
ECON 862.subject: ECON
ECON 862.title: International Monetary Economics

ECON 865.description: Examination of industrial pricing, output, and investment practices in relation to the theory of the firm. Consideration of public aspects of these practices.
ECON 865.subject: ECON
ECON 865.title: Industrial Organization

ECON 870.description: Topics studied include wage theory; the processes of wage determination; the impact of unions and collective bargaining on wage levels, prices, employment, and income distribution; bargaining theory and union-management relations; the union as an economic institution.
ECON 870.subject: ECON
ECON 870.title: Labor Economics I

ECON 872.description: A descriptive and analytic study of manpower as an economic resource in the United States.
ECON 872.subject: ECON
ECON 872.title: Labor Economics II

ECON 875.description: A survey of the contribution of economics to educational issues, including the value of educational investments, effect of education on economic growth, input-output analysis, and economics of educational finance.
ECON 875.subject: ECON
ECON 875.title: Economics of Education

ECON 880.description: A general survey of public finance, including public expenditures; the structure, incidence, and effects of taxes; public goods; and fiscal federalism.
ECON 880.subject: ECON
ECON 880.title: Public Finance I

ECON 882.description: An analysis of budgets and budget policy; tax incidence and effects; debt and debt management.
ECON 882.subject: ECON
ECON 882.title: Public Finance II

ECON 885.description: An analysis of economic forces affecting urbanization and the economic processes influencing urban form and structure. Spatial concepts are considered in addition to the traditional microeconomic and macroeconomic concepts.
ECON 885.subject: ECON
ECON 885.title: Urban Economics

ECON 886.description: Spatial and economic structures of regions and regional economic development. Topical review of partial and general equilibrium models of land use, regional economic growth; income determination at a regional level (regional accounts and input-output models); regional policy alternatives and their efficiency.
ECON 886.subject: ECON
ECON 886.title: Location Theory

ECON 891.description: Statistical designs and techniques for survey investigations. Mathematical development of sampling systems; sampling units; sample size; estimation; costs; non-sampling problems. Methods of obtaining and reporting information.
ECON 891.subject: ECON
ECON 891.title: Sampling Techniques

ECON 892.description: Research methods in Economics. The design and execution of a research paper in Economics. Preparation for writing a dissertation in Economics.
ECON 892.subject: ECON
ECON 892.title: Third-Year Seminar 1

ECON 893.description: Research methods in Economics. The design and execution of a research paper in Economics. Preparation for writing a dissertation in Economics.
